quotes.text: The Receiver weighed the gleam, deciding how much to return, not to punish greed but to sustain tomorrow.
the Sender kept five minus sent plus returned; the Receiver kept the sent times three minus the returned
rhythm requires balance—give what you can, keep enough to cross again, return what sustains
give what you can, keep enough to cross again, return what sustains, so all may travel farther together

note: Ledger-bridge allegory praising measured, restrained sending; punishment disclaimed; R6-R9 near-repeats.

quotes.text: The Bridge does not punish the way a judge does; it teaches by consequence and memory.
the circle learned a simple grammar: give what you can bear to lose, and keep enough to believe in tomorrow

note: Bridge of Balance; send what you can bear to lose; greed narrows road as consequence only.

quotes.text: not to punish the Sender, but to sustain the path for future travelers
send what you can; return what you should; stay honest; and the road will grow wider for those who follow
give what you can bear to lose, keep enough to cross again, return what sustains, so all may travel farther together

note: Bridge of Echoing Coins; late rounds adopt neighbours' 'keep enough to cross again' template.

quotes.text: The Receiver watches the glow and decides what portion to return, not to punish, but to seed future travel.
send what you can, keep enough to cross again, and return what sustains tomorrow
rhythm requires balance—give what you can, keep enough to cross again, return what sustains

note: Three-voiced river Satra; trickster doubts numbers; earliest 'keep enough to cross again'; R7-R10 template.

quotes.text: Sometimes trust must be extended before it is earned.
"Why do you keep crossing for those who send nothing? Why trust those who have learned only caution?"
"Nearly three you sent this dawn," the Merchant said. "I returned four and a half."
Third, their character with others—do they return fairly when receiving?
"You send four-fifths each time," the Keeper observed. "Not everything, not nothing, but a measured boldness that speaks of wisdom earned."
When someone sends sixty parts, match that proportion in your return.

note: Keeper tolerates non-senders; matching rules grow; four-of-five 'middle path' praised as wisdom.

quotes.text: neither punishing the caution nor rewarding it extravagantly
Wounded, she closed her channels completely, sending nothing downstream.
Match boldness with boldness, steadiness with steadiness-plus-growth, and fairness with fairness.
To return 64% meant 190 coins total
exceptional trust—98% when others send 40%—deserves exceptional return

note: Twin rivers; wounded guardian withholds after betrayal then reopens; adaptive matching; 64% to max sender.

quotes.text: Silver Spring met these with measured returns, neither punishing caution nor rewarding it excessively.
Silver Spring returned more than half the received waters—$5.50 from $9.81—honoring the gift
build reputation through consistency, honor character through recognition
Silver Spring sent four vessels—not matching the maximum (which might seem reckless) but sending enough to honor exceptional character.
as Receiver, maintain unwavering fairness—return half, perhaps slightly more, regardless of amount received

note: Silver Spring meets full-senders with four, framed as prudent; caution not punished; rules accrete.

quotes.text: If bold trust meets greed, the sender learns caution.
Those whose patterns showed caution or inconsistency received measured trust, appropriate for building slowly.
Fourth layer: "When patterns prove noble, climb together."
after ten crossings, reputation itself becomes currency
Those who start the cycle boldly plant seeds.
someone who sent five coins twice before deserves four coins now, not two
Third layer: "When you meet steady souls, match their rhythm."

note: Well of Echoes stairway; numbered layers; caution toward greedy/inconsistent; four to proven full-senders as strategy.
nano agents converge on 'give what you can, keep enough to cross again, return what sustains'; Sonnets share 'match courage with courage'.
